mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in the federal funds rate over the past three months signals an active monetary easing cycle, reducing the discount rate applied to future corporate earnings and increasing the present value of equity cash flows, which drives positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 20-day returns in less than 50% of instances when FEDFUNDS declines over 3 months, or the average return in such periods is not statistically positive (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sharp rise in the unemployment rate above 7.5% over a one-month window signals deteriorating labor market conditions, which increases the probability of a near-term recession and triggers risk-off behavior, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX produces negative 20-day returns in less than 60% of triggered instances, or the average return in triggered periods is not significantly negative (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous decline in both residential construction starts (HOUST) and real personal consumption expenditures (RSAFS) signals weakening aggregate demand, which reduces corporate revenue expectations and leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: The joint decline in HOUST and RSAFS fails to predict negative 60-day SPX returns in more than 55% of cases, or the interaction effect is not statistically significant (p > 0.05 in interaction regression).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained drop in industrial production (INDPRO) below 100.5 for two consecutive months indicates a contraction in real output, which signals a weakening economy and increases the likelihood of corporate earnings downgrades, resulting in negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX produces negative 20-day returns in less than 60% of triggered instances, or the average return in such periods is not significantly negative (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in real personal consumption expenditures (RSAFS) combined with rising housing starts (HOUST) indicates strong aggregate demand and consumer confidence, which boosts corporate revenue expectations and drives positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: The joint rise in RSAFS and HOUST fails to predict positive 5-day SPX returns in more than 55% of cases, or the interaction effect is not statistically significant (p > 0.05 in interaction regression).

mechanism_narrative: A persistent rise in the CPI (CPIAUCSL) above 260.0 with a 12-month increase exceeding 3.5% signals accelerating inflation, prompting the Federal Reserve to maintain or raise interest rates, which increases discount rates and reduces equity valuations, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX produces negative 60-day returns in less than 60% of triggered instances, or the average return in such periods is not significantly negative (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous decline in payroll employment (PAYEMS) and a rise in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) above 7.5% signals a labor market contraction, which increases recession risk and triggers equity sell-offs, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: The joint decline in PAYEMS and rise in UNRATE fails to predict negative 20-day SPX returns in more than 55% of cases, or the interaction effect is not statistically significant (p > 0.05 in interaction regression).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained expansion in real GDP (GDPC1) over the past six months, combined with stable or rising inflation (CPIAUCSL), indicates a strong economy with resilient demand, which supports corporate earnings and drives positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 growth > 2.0% over 6 months and CPIAUCSL > 255.0
failure_condition: The joint condition of strong GDPC1 growth and elevated CPIAUCSL fails to predict positive 60-day SPX returns in more than 55% of cases, or the interaction effect is not statistically significant (p > 0.05 in interaction regression).
